# TODO: v26, "After Wheaton"

Goal: republish this codebase as **After Wheaton** (v26), a satirical/parody app that still lets people check the SAGA (Anderson Commons) menu, repurposes Who's Who as a directory of trustees, donors, faculty, and administrators, and drops every feature that needs a Wheaton login, as well as any other security risks.

Reviewed: `master` @ `e5f081f` ("Version 3.3.0, currently published in the app store", 2016-01-19). Endpoint checks were run on 2026-10-11.

**Status (2026-10-11):** builds in Xcode 26.6 with no CocoaPods and runs on the iOS 26.5 simulator (iPhone 17 Pro). All five tabs load without crashing. Home shows the search bar and the empty Chapel/Sports dashboard, Events is empty (dead backends), Meal Menu shows the live Bon Appétit page, Map shows campus with no pins, and Extras lists its rows. In Debug builds, `-AWInitialTab N` (0-4) opens a given tab at launch, for screenshots via `xcrun simctl launch booted io.github.jackbandy.afterwheaton -AWInitialTab 2`.

## 0. Blockers: resolve before writing code

- [ ] **No license in the repo.** There's no `LICENSE` file, and most of the code isn't yours: by commit count, Chris Anderson has 73, Drew Hannay 42, `support` 13, you 10. File headers say `Copyright (c) 2013 Chris Anderson. All rights reserved.` Get written permission from the original authors (and possibly from Wheaton College, which shipped 3.3.0 under its own distribution cert), or rewrite the parts you keep. The menu-only scope below is small enough that a clean rewrite is realistic.
- [ ] **The name "After Wheaton" still contains "Wheaton".** App Review 4.1(c): "You cannot use another developer's icon, brand, or product name in your app's icon or name, without approval from the developer." And 5.2.1: "Don't use protected third-party material such as trademarks, copyrighted works, or patented ideas in your app without permission, and don't include misleading, false, or copycat representations, names, or metadata in your app bundle or developer name." (Source: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/, last updated June 8, 2026.) The parody framing doesn't exempt this. The satirist exemption in 1.1.1 covers "mean-spirited content," not trademarks. Decide whether to ask the college, accept the rejection risk, or pick a name without "Wheaton."
- [ ] **Permission for the menu data.** The old menu endpoint is dead (see §2). The live source is Bon Appétit's site: https://wheaton.cafebonappetit.com/cafe/anderson-commons/. App Review 5.2.2: "If your app uses, accesses, monetizes access to, or displays content from a third-party service, ensure that you are specifically permitted to do so under the service's terms of use. Authorization must be provided upon request." Read Bon Appétit's terms, and get permission in writing if possible.
- [ ] **Minimum functionality risk.** If the app is just a web view of the Bon Appétit page, it can be rejected under 4.2: "Your app should include features, content, and UI that elevate it beyond a repackaged website." Parsing the menu natively and adding the parody content helps.

## 1. Remove authenticated and personal-data features

- [x] **Banner login.** Deleted `BannerLoginViewController.{h,m}`, which stored the Banner username and PIN in the keychain and posted them to `bannerweb.wheaton.edu`. The `BannerLogin` storyboard scene still exists without its class (see "Orphaned storyboard scenes").
- [x] **GSKeychain.** Deleted.
- [x] **Login entry points.** Removed the "Banner → Login" section from Extras and the "SKIPS >" link on Home.
- [x] **Who's Who login dependency.** Home now searches a bundled `whoswho.json` locally (currently an empty `[]`; filling it is §1a). Records use `firstName`, `lastName`, `group`, `title`, `sourceUrl`, and `photo`.
- [x] **"Wink" / favorites.** The POST to `c_Favorites` and the Mixpanel calls are gone. Favorites now stay on the device. Keeping "Wink" as a parody gag is still your call.
- [x] **Push notifications.** Removed APNs registration, the device-token POST, `NotificationOptionsTableViewController`, `PushNotification`, and the "Notification Toggles" row. The `NotificationOptions` storyboard scene remains.
- [ ] **Orphaned storyboard scenes.** Delete scenes that point at login-era features: `DegreeEvaluation`, `AccountTable`, `ImportCalendar`, `NewTop`, `PastHome`, and `AccountTableViewCell`.
- [x] **Reachability.** Deleted `MTReachabilityManager`. Who's Who no longer waits for campus Wi-Fi.

## 1a. Repurpose Who's Who: trustees, donors, faculty, administration

- [ ] **Bundled dataset.** Replace the network search with a dataset shipped in the app, kept in the repo as the editable source (e.g. `data/whoswho.csv`, built into JSON). Search runs locally, with no server.
- [ ] **Record fields.** Name, group (Trustee / Donor / Faculty / Administration), title or role, department or committee, years, `source_url`, and `retrieved` date. No personal emails, phone numbers, home addresses, or student records.
- [ ] **Public sources only, cited per record.**
  - Trustees and senior leadership: the college's own published board and leadership pages.
  - Officers, trustees, and highest-paid staff: the college's IRS Form 990 (e.g. via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer).
  - Faculty: public faculty profile pages.
  - Donors: only donors the college itself publicly recognizes (named buildings, endowed chairs, published honor rolls). Don't infer gift amounts.
- [ ] **Donor caution.** Many donors are private individuals. App Review 1.1.1 flags content "particularly if the app is likely to humiliate, intimidate, or harm a targeted individual or group." Keep satire aimed at the institution and public roles, and add a correction/removal contact in the app.
- [ ] **UI reuse.** Keep `WhosWhoDetailViewController`, `WhoswhoSearchBar`, `WhoswhoTableCell` (+ `.xib`), and `Person`. Replace the student fields (`Classification`, `IdCardNum`, the `Type == "2"` filter in `HomeViewController.m`) with group/role, add a group filter, and show the source link on each detail page.
- [ ] **Photos.** Use them only where the source's license allows; otherwise show initials.

## 6. Modernize the toolchain

The project was last built around 2016 (Xcode 7 era) and won't build in current Xcode as-is.

- [x] **Deployment target.** Now iOS 17.0. The obsolete `GCC_VERSION = llvmgcc42` settings were also removed.
- [x] **Swift.** `RecordArticlesViewController.swift` and `XMLParser.swift` were ported to Swift 5. The parser class is now `RSSFeedParser`, and the Record feed URL is HTTPS.
- [x] **CocoaPods.** Removed entirely: the `Podfile`, the workspace, the Pods build phases, and the xcconfigs. AFNetworking became `NSURLSession` (`Utilities loadImageAtURL:…`). Reachability, LVDebounce, and TEAChart were dropped. iOS-blur became `UIVisualEffectView`, and UIView+AutoLayout became layout anchors. Explicit SDK framework links were also removed; module auto-linking handles them.
- [ ] **Deprecated APIs.** `UISearchDisplayController` crashes on iOS 26 at storyboard load, so it was removed. Home and Map now drive their own results table from `UISearchBarDelegate`. The private `_searchField` KVC was replaced with `searchTextField`. `UIAlertView` remains in `WhosWhoDetailViewController` and `BannerScrollView.h`.
- [x] **Launch screen.** Added an empty `UILaunchScreen` dict to Info.plist, which ends the letterboxed compatibility mode. The `LaunchImage` assets and `Default*.png` are now unused and can be deleted.
- [ ] **ATS.** Remove `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads = true` from Info.plist once every URL is HTTPS.
- [x] **Signing.** Removed the old team (`T7TBP7XHVC`), the John Hayward and Terry Perciante identities, both profile UUIDs, and the reference to a missing `Entitlements.plist`. All configurations now use automatic signing with "Apple Development".
- [ ] **Pick your team.** In Xcode, go to Signing & Capabilities and choose your team. `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` is blank, and this Mac has no signing certificates or Xcode accounts yet.
- [ ] **Push capability.** `TargetAttributes` still lists `com.apple.Push`. Remove it now that push code is gone.
- [ ] **Project format.** Run Xcode's "Update to recommended settings". The project still has `LastUpgradeCheck = 0500` and `objectVersion = 46`.
- [ ] **Tests.** `Wheaton AppTests` is the Xcode template. Add at least one test for the menu parser.
